correctness.rationale: Every finite \(n\ge1\) is covered by a row-stochastic Bernstein definition. A level-set proof gives the weighted Gini inequality; Jensen turns the column weights into an operator upper bound. An exact superlevel interval count plus the Bernstein basis peak monotonicity proves that the maximal column mass is the endpoint sum \(U_n\). The endpoint impulse has ratio \(R_n\), which exceeds one for all \(n\ge3\) by symmetric pair positivity. At \(n=1,2\) the norm is one. Dominated convergence makes both \(U_n\) and \(R_n\) converge to \(e/(e-1)\), with an explicit \(O(n^{-1})\) gap \(U_n-R_n\). Exact rational exhaustive checks cover 1,002 binary cuts in degrees \(n=2,\ldots,8\). No finite computation is used to justify the infinite statements.

value.rationale: The natural Gini seminorm measures the total pairwise dispersion of discretized profiles, distinct from local adjacent variation. The theorem proves the first dimension in which Bernstein smoothing amplifies it, proves amplification persists at every subsequent degree despite classical TV diminution, and determines the sharp dimension-limit norm \(e/(e-1)\). An explicit \(O(n^{-1})\) finite-degree sandwich gives non-asymptotic information about closeness of a natural impulse to the true (not assumed known) operator optimum; this is a structural operator-stability result, not a numerical curiosity.
